title: Correlate config/model drift with evals signals and provide unified, deduped alerts in Console (Slack / PagerDuty)
creator: Miguel Torres
description:
Problem: Evals detect quality regressions (example: drop in ROUGE/accuracy or semantic drift) but signals are noisy and disconnected from the deployment/config changes that often cause them. Customers get duplicate Slack/PagerDuty alerts when the same regression triggers across multiple models or rollout stages.

Goal: Produce a single, actionable regression alert in Console that: (1) correlates eval signal spikes with recent model/config changes (rollouts, quantization profiles, batching changes), (2) groups related signals across models/variants/tenants, and (3) sends deduped notifications to Slack and PagerDuty with traceable context and recommended remediation steps.

Scope: Backend correlator service + Console UI (alerts timeline + signal grouping) + Alerting integration updates for Slack/PagerDuty. This ticket covers PM work, acceptance criteria, stakeholder coordination with ENG and DX (design), and initial rollout plan for Canary customers.
acceptance_criteria: Console alerts show a single grouped regression event when the same eval suite fails across >1 model variant within the configured dedupe window
Each alert includes correlated metadata: model version, config diff (key changed), rollout id, timestamp of rollout, top failing prompts, and link to failing eval runs
Slack notification format includes short summary, severity, link to Console incident, and action buttons (mute/acknowledge/open runbook)
PagerDuty mapping created: regressed signal -> escalation policy, with suppression during active canary window if configured
Engineers can toggle dedupe window and grouping heuristics per-project in Console and see retrospective reconstructions in the Eval timeline
No more than 2x baseline alert volume for the pilot orgs after rollout; feedback loop from pilot shows reduced triage time by >=30%
Automated tests validate grouping logic with synthetic eval runs and simulated model rollouts
